# Introduction

MetaboReport provides step-by-step guidance on each page to help you perform a data analysis.

MetaboReport accepts a variety of outputs produced by different software tools, such as **XCMS**, **MSDIAL**, and **Compound Discoverer**. The output table can be submitted to MetaboReport with very little modification.

MetaboReport requires two types of information: **peak-area data** and **sample metadata**.

> `Peak area`: the integrated area under a chromatographic peak. It is commonly used as a relative measure of feature abundance. Depending on the data-processing software, peak intensity or peak height may be reported instead.
>
> `Sample metadata`: labels or group information that describe each sample.

There are **two ways** to prepare input data for MetaboReport:

> **1**. Peak-area data and metadata are stored in the same table. Upload one table.
>
> **2**. Peak-area data and metadata are stored in separate tables. Upload both tables.

This manual explains how to prepare both input formats.

# Data Preparation

Input tables can be CSV (`.csv`) or Microsoft Excel (`.xls` or `.xlsx`) files.

## Demo Data

The following example shows how to prepare an input table for MetaboReport.

Suppose you want to compare metabolic profiles between wild-type (**WT**) and mutant (**MU**) mice. Each biological sample is therefore labeled as either **WT** or **MU**.

Suppose sex is also relevant to the study, so a second metadata field records each biological sample as `Male` or `Female`.

Pooled QC (`QC`) samples are included to monitor analytical variation.

This study contains two metadata fields: Group 1 contains WT, MU, and QC; Group 2 contains Male, Female, and QC. Each sample therefore has two labels. For example, Sample_3 is WT and Male, whereas Sample_13 is QC in both fields (Table 1).

\newpage

**Table 1**. Experiment design of a metabolomics study.

| Sample   | Sample Label 1 | Sample Label 2 |
|----------|----------------|----------------|
| Sample_1  | WT             | Male           |
| Sample_2  | WT             | Female         |
| Sample_3  | WT             | Male           |
| ...       | ...            | ...            |
| Sample_12 | MU             | Female         |
| Sample_13 | QC             | QC             |
| Sample_16 | QC             | QC             |

The study contains 16 samples (Table 1). After LC-MS analysis and data processing, you may obtain a table like Table 2. Each row represents a mass feature, and the columns contain feature descriptors or sample peak areas.

**Table 2**. An example of sample-feature table.

| mz       | Retention Time | Identification | PeakArea of Sample_1 | PeakArea of Sample_2 | .... | PeakArea of Sample_16 |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| 133.014  | 3.23           | Malic acid     | 123000              | 120000              | ...  | 801000               |
| 144.012  | 2.44           | Unknown        | 678555              | 666000              | ...  | 1200                 |
| 333.331  | 10.18          | Unknown        | 3400                | 2000                | ...  | 560000               |
| 234.446  | 5.52           | Unknown        | 45000               | 55000               | ...  | 46000                |
| ...      | ...            | ...            | ...                 | ...                 | ...  | ...                  |
| 1034.552 | 25.33          | Tomatine       | 4780                | 4300                | ...  | 12000                |


Table 2 must be modified to create an input table for MetaboReport.

As described above, there are two supported input formats.

## Method 1: Peak-area data and metadata in one table

For Method 1, rename all peak-area columns shown in Table 2.

For example, rename `PeakArea of Sample_1` to `Sample_WT_Male_1`. See Table 3.

If the sample-feature table was generated by Compound Discoverer, `PeakArea of Sample_1` may instead be renamed `WT_Male_1`. The **Sample** prefix is optional for the Compound Discoverer format.

**Explanation**:

> -   Add the case-sensitive prefix `Sample_` to every peak-area column so MetaboReport can recognize it.
> -   Sample_1 has two metadata values (Table 1), so **WT** and **Male** follow `Sample_` and are separated by underscores. Metadata values are case-sensitive; for example, **WT** and **wt** are treated as different groups.
> -   Add a unique number after the metadata to distinguish sample replicates.

\newpage

**Table 3**. Sample-Feature table for MetaboReport prepared by method 1.

| mz       | Sample_WT_Male_1 | Sample_WT_Female_2 | Sample_QC_QC_16 |
|----------|------------------|--------------------|-----------------|
| 133.014  | 123000           | 120000             | 801000          |
| 144.012  | 678555           | 666000             | 1200            |

> **Note:** You may apply this naming convention to raw-data filenames before data processing so that the resulting sample-feature table can be used directly by MetaboReport.

## Method 2: Peak-area data and metadata in separate tables

Method 2 requires a separate metadata table.

For **peak area table**:

> -   Name every peak-area column using the case-sensitive format `Sample_<number>` so MetaboReport can recognize it (for example, `Sample_1`, `Sample_2`).
> -   Other columns are optional and may remain in the table.
> -   The peak-area table may also use the full naming convention described in Method 1.

See Table 4 for details.

**Table 4**. Peak area table for MetaboReport prepared by method 2.

| mz       | Retention Time | Identification | Sample_1 | Sample_2 | .... | Sample_16 |
|----------|----------------|----------------|---------|---------|------|----------|
| 133.014  | 3.23           | Malic acid     | 123000  | 120000  | ...  | 801000   |
| 144.012  | 2.44           | Unknown        | 678555  | 666000  | ...  | 1200     |
| 333.331  | 10.18          | Unknown        | 3400    | 2000    | ...  | 560000   |
| 234.446  | 5.52           | Unknown        | 45000   | 55000   | ...  | 46000    |
| ...      | ...            | ...            | ...     | ...     | ...  | ...      |
| 1034.552 | 25.33          | Tomatine       | 4780    | 4300    | ...  | 12000    |

For **Metadata table**:

> Prepare a separate table that describes the metadata for each sample (Table 5). Column headers may use any names, but the first column must contain sample identifiers. Metadata values are case-sensitive, so use them consistently.

**Table 5**. Metadata table for MetaboReport prepared by method 2.

| Sample   | Sample Label 1 | Sample Label 2 |
|----------|----------------|----------------|
| Sample_1  | WT             | Male           |
| Sample_2  | WT             | Female         |
| Sample_3  | WT             | Male           |
| ...       | ...            | ...            |
| Sample_12 | MU             | Female         |
| Sample_13 | QC             | QC             |
| Sample_16 | QC             | QC             |

**Important:** MetaboReport currently assigns metadata by row order. Use the same `Sample_<number>` identifiers in Tables 4 and 5, and list them in exactly the same order. Otherwise, metadata will be assigned to the wrong samples.


# Demo Data

Two demo datasets, prepared using Methods 1 and 2, are available from the **Home** page of the MetaboReport app.

Use these demo datasets as references when preparing your own data.

# Common Mistakes

**1. My data table is not accepted or not recognized by MetaboReport.**

Most import errors result from an unsupported input format. Check the following points when preparing a data table:

> - Metadata values are case-sensitive. For example, **WT**, **Wt**, and **wt** are treated as different groups, so use labels consistently.
> 
> - `Sample_` is the reserved, case-sensitive prefix used by MetaboReport to recognize **peak-area** columns. For Method 2, use the exact format `Sample_<number>`.
>
> - **QC** is a reserved keyword used only for QC samples.
>
> - Avoid unintended **white space**. `WT` and <code>WT&nbsp;</code> are treated as different metadata values.
> 
> - For tables generated by **Compound Discoverer**, export all `Area` columns and select `Compound Discoverer (CD)` on the **Upload Data** page. For tables produced by other software, select `Other format`.

**2. It takes too long to generate the report.**

> - Additional calculations are performed during report generation, so the process may take a few minutes.
> 
> - If report generation fails, restart the app session and rerun the analysis.
